messages:
jen (Customer): Hey team — since the corp proxy change last night our on-prem service (Redwood Private) is failing to call the API. We're seeing intermittent TLS handshake errors and 502s. Example curl we run through our forward proxy:

```bash
curl -v -x http://proxy.corp:8080 "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxxx' \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

Response snippet:

```
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.10.10.2) port 8080 (#0)
* Proxy replied 200 TO CONNECT
* TLS handshake error:
  x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
```

Header we captured: `x-rw-request-id: rw_abc123`. We're in a no-internet mode except via our corp forward proxy. Any quick checks?

sarah (Support): Thanks, jen — sorry about the disruption. A few quick clarifying q's: are you running Redwood Private on VMs you manage (on-prem containers/nodes) or on Dedicated hosted by us? Also please paste the full curl -v output and, if possible, the output of:

```bash
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai
```

run from a host behind the proxy (or proxied via socat) so we can see the presented chain.

james (Solutions): FWIW this looks like typical TLS interception (MITM) by the forward proxy. Two common failure modes we see: 1) proxy presents corporate CA cert that isn't trusted by the runtime, 2) proxy doesn't do a true CONNECT tunnel (or strips SNI/ALPN) causing a broken handshake.

Quick repro set:
1) `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/health` and paste the full output.
2) `openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp:8080 -proxy proxy.corp:8080 -servername api.redwood.ai` — if the proxy is intercepting you will see the issuer as your corp CA, not Redwood.
3) From a bastion with direct egress: `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai` should show Redwood's cert chain.

If MITM is in play you have two safe options: install corp CA into the trust store used by your Redwood nodes, or configure the proxy to bypass TLS inspection for the Redwood hostnames (SNI-based bypass / CONNECT passthrough).

mike (NetOps): In our environment BlueProxy v3 does TLS inspection by default and we can add SNI bypass rules. Tell me the FQDNs and we'll add them. @sarah do you have the canonical list of endpoints?

sarah (Support): Yes — canonical hostnames to allowlist/bypass: `api.redwood.ai`, `auth.redwood.ai`, `uploads.redwood.ai`, `models-cdn.redwood.ai`. We'll also push a short egress IP list to the support portal for your firewall/network team. In the meantime you can test a bypass by SSHing to a bastion and setting `HTTPS_PROXY` there and running the same curl. If you choose to install CA into containers: on Debian containers run `update-ca-certificates`, and for Java runtimes import the PEM into the JVM keystore:

```bash
keytool -import -trustcacerts -alias corp-proxy-ca -file /tmp/corp-ca.pem -keystore $JAVA_HOME/lib/security/cacerts -storepass changeit
```

(james: note the default password is `changeit` — change after import).

jen (Customer): We tried dropping corp CA into system certs inside the container but still saw intermittent `upstream handshake error: remote error: tls: internal error` in our app logs. It seems like some connections succeed and some fail — possibly connection reuse/keepalive with the proxy.

james (Solutions): That pattern often indicates the proxy is not cleanly tunneling multiple connections (or is terminating keepalive then presenting a different cert). Quick tests to isolate: force HTTP/1.1 so we bypass HTTP/2 multiplexing on the proxy:

```bash
curl --http1.1 --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

If that reduces failures it points at HTTP/2/connection reuse handling in the proxy. Also collect a tcpdump during a failed handshake and share (pcap) — look for `ClientHello`/`ServerHello` sequences and who is actually answering.

jen (Customer): I ran the `--http1.1` test and over a 30m run the failures dropped to near zero. Good temporary mitigation.

sarah (Support): Great. We'll escalate for an SNI bypass. Mike, can you create a ticket and add SNI bypass entries for the domains above? Also please confirm when the rollout starts so customer can re-run tests.

mike (NetOps): Creating INFRA-7890 now — adding SNI bypass for `api.redwood.ai`, `auth.redwood.ai`, `uploads.redwood.ai`, `models-cdn.redwood.ai`. Rollout planned to all forward proxies in 30 minutes; ETA for completion 45m. Will post logs after smoke test.

deploy-bot: INFRA-7890 rollout started -> phase 1: deploy bypass rule to proxy-edge-1..3.

jen (Customer): After the SNI bypass was applied I can confirm errors disappeared and our production traffic is stable. Thanks! One ask from our security folks: they prefer not to install our corp CA into customer-managed nodes. Can you provide a short KB we can hand to them explaining why a bypass is necessary and safe?

sarah (Support): On it. Short summary we'll include in KB: TLS inspection breaks end-to-end integrity and can interfere with token-based auth and certificate pinning; recommended approach is SNI-based bypass for well-scoped hostnames, combined with narrow egress allowlist and strict firewall rules on IPs. We'll attach the exact commands we used to repro and a checklist for NetOps.

jen (Customer): Perfect — thanks everyone :tada:

sarah (Support): Marking this thread for follow-up KB, closing once KB is posted. If anything reappears ping us and we'll reopen.
